id: ocr-comparison
genre: references
title: "Local OCR vs remote OCR API — benchmark notes"
created: 2026-03-10
provenance: hand-authored
tags: [ocr, benchmark]
source: "internal benchmark notes, Q1 tooling review"
---

Comparing local OCR against a remote OCR API on sample scans: the remote API
sustained roughly four times the local throughput at a per-page cost the
studio could absorb, with better layout detection on old typefaces.
Assumption on record: throughput scales linearly with scan volume.

Informed d-004. The linearity assumption is what s-006 later challenged.

The Foxglove Archive is a digitized-collection platform for Harrowgate
Press: scanning, OCR, searchable metadata, and an online gallery. The OCR
pipeline runs on a local GPU cluster rather than a remote API (decision
d-104); the throughput benchmark (s-113) showed modern scans running above
the assumed rate, which kept the digitization schedule. The viewer is a
static-file gallery (decision d-113), prototyped in s-122, with page-level
anchor URLs added in June (d-118).

Team: Marta Quintana (data), Gwen Torvald (interface), Yusuf Adeyemi (OCR
pipeline), Elif Yilmaz (user research). Aurelio Finch is the client sponsor;
Saltmarsh Creative advised the metadata descriptions. Mid-project review
with Harrowgate is m-112.

As of late June the project is active: the modern collection is scanned, the
annex queue is staged for summer, and the gallery is in integration.

The Larkspur Archive is a digitized-collection platform for Bellweather
Books: scanning, OCR, searchable metadata, and an online viewer. The OCR
pipeline uses a remote OCR API over local OCR (decision d-004, informed by
the ocr-comparison notes); a later latency benchmark (s-006) showed archival
page scans running far below the assumed throughput, which sent Dev and
Silas back to preprocessing. The viewer is IIIF-based (decision d-011),
prototyped in s-010.

Team: Silas Brandt (data), June Park (interface), Dev Okonkwo (OCR pipeline),
Odessa Klein (user research). Rowan Ellery is the client sponsor; Quill &
Marrow advised the metadata descriptions. Mid-project review with Bellweather
is m-007.

As of mid-June the project is active: OCR continues at the corrected rate and
the IIIF viewer is in integration.

MQTT 5.0 keeps retained messages — a display recovers its last-known state
after reconnect — and adds shared subscriptions that fan one topic across
several consumers, plus session expiry and reason codes that make reconnects
observable. Broker overhead is the cost; for small realtime payloads it
still beats HTTP polling on freshness and battery.

decision (d-108).

WAL mode gives readers concurrent access while a single writer appends; crash
recovery is simple and the whole datastore is one file. Trade-off: a
single-writer ceiling, so it fits services with modest write volume — exactly
the profile of a studio billing tool.

Informed the Ledgerline datastore decision (d-001).
